artworks.title: Ulysses and the Sirens
artworks.description: Waterhouse's Siren lure — the song that in Apollonius' Argonautica pulls Butes son of Teleon overboard while Orpheus sings against it. National Gallery of Victoria.

artworks.title: Odysseus and the Sirens (the "Siren Vase")
artworks.description: Attic red-figure name-vase of the Siren episode — the same peril Butes alone fails among the Argonauts, saved by Aphrodite at Lilybaeum.

artworks.title: The Birth of Venus
artworks.description: Botticelli's Venus — the goddess who, in Apollonius, lifts drowning Butes from the Sirens' sea and sets him ashore in western Sicily.

popCulture.title: Butes
popCulture.description: Athenian Argonaut, son of Teleon, who leapt toward the Sirens and was saved by Aphrodite — not Butes son of Pandion, the Erechtheid priest.

popCulture.title: Argonautica
popCulture.creator: Apollonius of Rhodes
popCulture.description: Apollonius' voyage: Orpheus out-sings the Sirens while Butes alone jumps — the Athenian as the crew's single failure of will.

popCulture.title: Jason and the Argonauts
popCulture.creator: Don Chaffey / Ray Harryhausen
popCulture.description: Harryhausen's screen Argonautica keeps the Siren peril in popular memory — Butes' leap as the literary twin of that danger.
